problem: End-to-end RL navigation agents keep memory in a GRU or in explicit grid/topological maps, which struggle to map object positions and scene structure compactly; explicit maps need discretisation and growing storage. Implicit neural fields had not been used dynamically as memory inside a downstream navigation policy.
motivation: Multi-Object Navigation requires remembering where previously seen objects are and which areas were explored or blocked, so that the agent can backtrack and explore efficiently. Neural implicit representations have a continuous nature, with detail controlled by a parameter budget, which suggests a compact and queryable memory that can be learned online during each episode.
key_idea: Structure an RL agent with two neural implicit representations trained online in each episode (a query-able Semantic Finder that outputs object positions, and an Occupancy and Exploration field read globally by a transformer that maps network weights to an embedding), and feed both to the policy.
insight: Both representations improve the agent. On MultiON test, the Semantic Finder gives the largest gain (Table 1: success 42.3 to 46.7, PPL 37.8 to 44.8, means), and adding occupancy helps further on val. Uncertainty estimation matters (Table 3: success 35.4 to 43.4, PPL 40.9 to 46.4). The gains are complementary to the auxiliary losses, and the per-episode SGD fitting does not appear to suffer catastrophic forgetting because of the replay buffers (Fig 5).
method: Semantic Finder fs: 3-layer MLP (512 hidden) mapping a 9-d class query (1-in-K with a background class) to a 3D object position. It is trained online with an L1 loss on points obtained by inverse-projecting the depth of a pre-trained segmentation model's output, using a replay buffer.

Uncertainty estimation: minimum Euclidean distance between the query and the queries in the scene replay buffer, giving a density-like unnormalised uncertainty that lets the agent discard unseen-object predictions.

Occupancy and Exploration field fo: a 2D top-down MLP on Fourier features that classifies Obstacle/Navigable/Unexplored. It is trained online with cross entropy from height-thresholded projected points, a balanced buffer of the last 1000 steps, and uniformly sampled Unexplored noisy labels.

Global reader r: a transformer (4 layers, 8 heads, CLS token) whose input tokens are the incoming weights of each neuron of fo with Fourier positional encodings. It outputs a 576-d embedding, favouring invariance to neuron permutation. It is pre-trained on 25k trajectories with a 3-step recipe (autoencoder on absolute maps, then reader on absolute maps, then finetuning on egocentric maps with pose fusion) and then frozen.

Agent: GRU policy trained with PPO whose inputs are the RGB-D encoding, previous action, goal, predicted position, uncertainty and global embedding. The representations are updated by SGD at every step (ns=1, no≤20), and gradients are not propagated through them.
Training curriculum: 0-30M steps without representations, 30-50M with fs, and 50-70M with both (used in the ablations); the SOTA comparison also trains without the curriculum.

setting.backbone: GRU RL policy (PPO) with a small CNN encoder, MLP implicit fields trained online, a transformer global reader and a CNN segmentation head; all trained from scratch or pre-trained on task data
setting.training_data: MultiON on Matterport3D (61 train scenes, 50k episodes per scene), 70M PPO steps; global reader on 25k baseline-agent trajectories; segmentation on 132k RGB-D/mask pairs; optional encoder pre-training and auxiliary losses from Marza et al. IROS 2022
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D 256x256 plus perfect GPS/compass odometry and goal class
setting.action_space: discrete: move forward 0.25 m, turn left/right 30°, Found
setting.privileged: Perfect odometry (agent pose and heading) at test time. During training only: object positions and segmentation masks from the simulator, plus auxiliary losses using privileged info in some variants.

numbers_note: MultiON is not among the canonical benchmark names, so it is listed as other:MultiON (3-ON). Table 1 also gives best-seed results (val success 43.1, test success 49.7, test PPL 45.9).
results: The full implicit-representation agent reaches test PPL 44.8 with a curriculum (vs. 37.8 NoMap and 40.1 ProjNMap with the same pre-training). Without a curriculum and with auxiliary losses it reaches 58.3 success and 52.1 PPL, vs. 57.7 success and 45.9 PPL for the previous best ProjNMap+AUX (winner of the CVPR 2021 challenge). Runs at ~45 fps in training.
limitations: RL training is slower than for the baselines (45 fps vs. 150-200 fps), and the uncertainty needs the full replay buffer.
The Semantic Finder handles only one instance per object class and provides only positions, not paths or distances.
It relies on perfect odometry and on simulator supervision during training (object positions, segmentation masks); only MultiON with coloured cylinders is evaluated.
builds_on: Teaching agents how to map (Marza et al. IROS 2022)
